thread:
eng-release: rolling deploy started for service-inference v3.2.1 -> canary on prod-us-east-1 (autorange 10%). monitoring only for 15m :eyes:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: svc-inference degraded in prod-us-east-1. Severity: P1. On-call: @sre_jamie. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-20260315-01
sre_jamie: seeing spike in 5xx from canary nodes, traces show KMS access denied errors when fetching model keys. quick log snippet: `ERROR: kms:Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException`
r en e: wait typo — sorry — rene: grabbing logs now, looks like env var KMS_KEY_ARN is pointing to a rotated key id that no longer exists in account-prod. requests that attempt to fetch model weights fail at init, 503s bubble up
eng-release: we just rolled a config change that updates KMS_KEY_ARN for v3.2.1. Canary should have used new key. Did the deploy apply IAM role changes?
ops_lead: checking iam diff... deploy step applied role-policy v2 which references kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/old-key-id — but key was rotated yesterday and alias updated. The policy still binds to old key id -> permission mismatch
sre_jamie: suggested mitigations: 1) kill canary feature flag to stop routing to new instances 2) rollback the release 3) quick patch: update env var to alias ARN that maps to current key (if safe)
eng-release: killing canary flag now — `./feature-flag set --service=service-inference canary_use_new_key false`
deploy-bot: Executed feature flag toggle by eng-release at 1785000032. Previous state: true -> false
eng-release: traffic routing switched back to stable -> instrumenting metrics to verify 5xx drop
cs_amy: heads up CS — some customers in the EU and NA regions might have seen failures for model fetch calls since 15:00 UTC. I can prep a short email if needed once we have impact numbers
rene: can we get count? Cloudwatch shows ~12k requests failed over the last 8m for prod-us-east-1, error 503, 7% of total requests for that interval. A subset (approx 400 req/min) returned KMS AccessDenied earlier
sre_jamie: I'll start rollback now. Command: `redwood deploy rollback --service service-inference --to stable-20260314-2300 --region us-east-1` — initiating at 1785000065
deploy-bot: Rollback started by sre_jamie at 1785000070. Estimated time to steady state: 3m
ops_lead: while rollback proceeds, I'm also opening a temporary allow policy to grant role decrypt on the alias `alias/service-inference-key` so even if env var mismatch exists new nodes can still use decrypt. Command I ran: `aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/service-inference-key --policy file://allow-decrypt.json` (policy is scoped to role-service-inference-prod)
sre_jamie: rollback finished at 1785000190. Canary instances drained, stable pods serving again. 5xx rate dropped back to baseline within ~40s. :white_check_mark:
eng-release: confirm service health dashboards look green for prod-us-east-1?
rene: health green, error rate back to 0.6% (normal). Latency normal. No CPU spike.
cs_amy: I'll notify affected customers with initial statement: apology, short description, mitigation (rollback), ETA for full postmortem. Draft in #customer-notifications for review
ops_lead: we need to fix root cause: two parallel changes — key rotation (yesterday) and deploy that used hard key id not alias. Short term: switch env to use alias ARN and update docs to require alias usage. Long term: add deploy validation that checks KMS key id exists & policy allows decrypt for the role before progressing past canary
sre_jamie: agree. Also recommend adding a preflight check in the deployment pipeline: `aws kms describe-key --key-id $KMS_KEY_ARN` and validate `KeyState == Enabled` and policy grants `kms:Decrypt` to the role. If check fails, fail canary and rollback automatically
eng-release: creating follow-up tasks: DEVOPS-1428 (deploy preflight KMS check), DEVOPS-1429 (change env var to alias usage), DEVOPS-1430 (postmortem writeup).
rene: tagging impacted customers: internal list shows 3 enterprise customers had >5% error rate: Acme Analytics, BrightCart, MemoPay. CS to own outreach.
cs_amy: sending notifications now, will include ask for impacted sessions logs and offer to extend credits. Posted to #customer-notifications at 1785000300
sre_jamie: handing incident to eng-release and ops_lead for remediation. I'll be on-call for follow-up for 30m then handing to next rotation.
sre_jamie: notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause = config used key-id (rotated) not alias; mitigation = kill canary flag + rollback + temporary key policy; impact = ~12k failed requests, 3 enterprise customers >5% errors; action items = DEVOPS-1428..1430
eng-release: thanks all. postmortem owner ops_lead. closing thread when postmortem created. :pray:
deploy-bot: Deploy rollback event closed at 1785000389
ops_lead: creating postmortem doc now, will ping when ready.
